verdicts.strongest_argument: Two things put this in the middle-upper band rather than the low one, and the second is the stronger. First, it is published in the corpus, and published by a service whose entire purpose is to surface exactly this: ceo-buys.com posts reproducing every transaction with size, price and resulting holding appear in two separate stored bodies (docs/efbcfae7dffa7859bd8b63014428f3765f25ef93.txt and docs/eaf570aeb2ef6c8dc678cbc913a1e7dfceac5654.txt), on top of the Form 4 index itself. A dedicated insider-buying aggregator republishing each purchase within days is not an unpublished fact; it is a syndicated one, and the hunter's own independence field describes two sources carrying it. Second, and decisively, the purchases are already in the price bars because they ARE the price bars. On 12,515 shares of average daily volume, a buyer taking down clips worth up to 74% of a session is the marginal bid, and the tape shows exactly that: run_up_5d +6.05% and run_up_20d +13.43% into the print, in a $23m ADR with 95.8% realised volatility. The claim that the market has not priced the CEO's conviction is contradicted by the fact that the CEO's own buying moved the stock 13% in twenty sessions. What is left is the forward question of whether she keeps buying, which the corpus cannot answer. The hunter is right that the dollar size is trivial - roughly 57,600 shares at about $2.15, some $124k, or half a percent of market capitalisation - and I agree with it that the argument has to be about frequency rather than magnitude, which makes it a sentiment inference rather than a quantity.

prior_publication.what_it_says: A public insider-buying aggregator publishes each of the eleven purchases with size, price and cumulative holding, and the posts are reproduced in two captured bodies before the print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Baseline (bmo print, so no 2026-09-03 bar): spot 2.28 at the 09-02 close, run_up_5d +6.05%, run_up_20d +13.43%, avg_volume_20d 12,515, realised_vol_20d 95.8%, pct_from_52w_low +31.79%. The stock is up 13% over the twenty sessions in which the buying occurred - the purchases and the run-up are the same event seen twice. Median print reaction 4.29% against a 2.15% deadband.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A purchase at a size that could not be absorbed by the tape - a block, a private placement, a 13D crossing - or evidence the buying continued after 09-01 at an accelerating pace, which would make it forward flow rather than a completed bid.

interactions: none - single finding, though the hunter's two 'independent' sources are two reproductions of the same ceo-buys.com feed, so they are one source.
corpus_limits: YQ's capture directory is dated 2026-09-02 against a 2026-09-03 event date, and the baseline is event_plausibility 'unknown' with cadence_implausible on a 64-day inferred cadence, so the 4.29% median expected move is not a reliable earnings base rate and I could not confirm from a company source in this capture that a results release occurred on 09-03 rather than earlier. No Form 4 body is stored; the transaction detail reaches me only through the aggregator posts. YQ carries no news items and the capture holds 30 items in total. I did not open docs/352e5565c8c4c0d3898f5a4ba5c6d316d29af018.txt.
